## Architecture at a glance

- QuotesDone is a UAE B2B anonymous quotation marketplace, run as an autonomous AI company.
- Backend: Supabase Postgres + 190 Deno/TypeScript edge functions + pg_cron.
- Frontend: Next.js in `src/`.
- Every LLM call routes through `supabase/functions/ai_gateway`, which applies rate limiting, a no-model FAQ layer, model-policy routing, deterministic refusals, department budget halts, and exact+semantic caching before any model is called.

## 1. AI cost control layer

Every model call in the company funnels through these files. `ai_gateway` is the single entry point; `_shared/llm.ts` is the client every other edge function uses to reach it; the migrations below define the routing, budget, caching and health tables and functions it reads.

### supabase/functions/ai_gateway/index.ts

```typescript
// ai_gateway — THE single AI router. Every model call in the company should come through here.
//
// WHY THIS EXISTS. Before it, ~68 edge functions called OpenRouter, 37 of them with their own
// hand-rolled fetch. Those 37 are invisible to ai_cost_log, so the company could not even see what
// it was spending, let alone control it. model_policy held 26 carefully written routing rules that
// had never executed once, because _shared/llm.ts only consults them when a caller passes taskClass
// and no caller did. The result: 100% of measured calls went to Sonnet or Opus, there was no cheap
// tier in existence, the cache had zero rows, and the budget halt was unreachable.
//
// This function is where all of that becomes real, in one place, so behaviour can change without
// redeploying 68 functions.
//
// ORDER OF OPERATIONS — cheapest possible outcome first, every time:
//   1. rate limit        - refuse abuse before spending anything
//   2. Level 0           - templates and the approved FAQ answer with NO model at all
//   3. routing           - fn_ai_route picks the tier from the calling function or task_class
//   4. refusal           - tier='none' means deterministic code is correct; we decline
//   5. budget halt       - department over its ceiling stops non-gated work
//   6. cache             - exact hash, then SEMANTIC similarity on free in-region embeddings
//   7. the call          - with Anthropic prompt caching, a hard token cap, and a model ladder
//   8. log               - real cost from model_registry, including cache-read pricing
//
// dry_run:true runs 1-6 and returns the decision WITHOUT calling a model, so the whole thing can be
// verified for zero spend.
import { createClient } from 'jsr:@supabase/supabase-js@2';

const admin = createClient(Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_URL')!, Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY')!);
const J = (o: unknown, s = 200) =>
  new Response(JSON.stringify(o), { status: s, headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } });

async function sec(k: string) {
  const { data } = await admin.from('app_secrets').select('value').eq('key', k).maybeSingle();
  return (data?.value as string) || '';
}
const secretOk = (v: unknown): v is string => typeof v === 'string' && v.trim().length >= 24;

// Free, in-region. Module scope on purpose: building the session per request is exactly what killed
// kb_embed with WORKER_RESOURCE_LIMIT on 28 Jul.
// deno-lint-ignore no-explicit-any
let _emb: any = null;
// deno-lint-ignore no-explicit-any
function embedder(): any {
  // deno-lint-ignore no-explicit-any
  if (_emb === null) _emb = new (globalThis as any).Supabase.ai.Session('gte-small');
  return _emb;
}
async function embed(text: string): Promise<string | null> {
  try {
    const v = await embedder().run(String(text).slice(0, 1200), { mean_pool: true, normalize: true }) as number[];
    return '[' + v.join(',') + ']';
  } catch (_e) { return null; }  // embedding is an optimisation; never fail the call for it
}

async function sha256(s: string): Promise<string> {
  const b = await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', new TextEncoder().encode(s));
  return Array.from(new Uint8Array(b)).map((x) => x.toString(16).padStart(2, '0')).join('');
}

// Anthropic bills a cached prefix at ~10% of the prompt rate but requires a minimum cacheable
// block. Below roughly 1k tokens the cache write costs more than it saves, so only mark long
// system prompts. This is the single biggest lever we have: 94% of spend is input tokens.
const CACHE_MIN_CHARS = 4000;

// supabase-js .rpc() returns a PostgrestFilterBuilder - it is thenable but NOT a Promise, so
// .catch() on it throws "admin.rpc(...).catch is not a function". Caught in dry-run testing.
// Every non-critical call (logging, cache writes) goes through here: telemetry must never be
// able to fail the business call it is describing.
async function rpcSafe(name: string, args: Record<string, unknown>) {
  try { const { data } = await admin.rpc(name, args); return data; } catch (_e) { return null; }
}

interface Body {
  __secret?: string;
  fn?: string; task_class?: string; dept?: string; agent?: string;
  sys?: string; input?: string | { role: string; content: string }[];
  max?: number; temperature?: number; confidence?: number;
  cache_ttl_min?: number; try_faq?: boolean; faq_text?: string;
  rate_key?: string; rate_limit?: number; rate_window_s?: number;
  stream?: boolean; dry_run?: boolean; escalate?: boolean;
  action?: string; text?: string;
}

Deno.serve(async (req) => {
  const t0 = Date.now();
  try {
    const body = (await req.json().catch(() => ({}))) as Body;
    const inbound = await sec('inbound_secret');
    if (!secretOk(inbound) || body.__secret !== inbound) return J({ error: 'forbidden' }, 403);

    // Utility path: embed text for callers that need a vector (FAQ backfill, semantic search).
    // Free, so it never touches routing or budget.
    if (body.action === 'embed') {
      const v = await embed(String(body.text || ''));
      return J({ ok: true, embedding: v });
    }

    const fnName = String(body.fn || 'unknown');
    const dry = body.dry_run === true;

    // ---- 1. RATE LIMIT ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Public surfaces (wa_inbound had none) must be capped before anything is spent.
    if (body.rate_key) {
      const { data: rl } = await admin.rpc('fn_rate_limit', {
        p_bucket: String(body.rate_key),
        p_limit: Number(body.rate_limit ?? 20),
        p_window_seconds: Number(body.rate_window_s ?? 3600),
      });
      if (rl && rl.allowed === false) {
        return J({ ok: true, used_llm: false, outcome: 'rate_limited', detail: rl });
      }
    }

    // ---- 2. LEVEL 0 — answer with no model at all ---------------------------------------
    // The plan's "70% should never reach AI". Templates and the 151 approved public FAQs.
    // Semantic matching included, because keyword search missed 2 of 5 realistic questions.
    if (body.try_faq) {
      const q = String(body.faq_text ?? (typeof body.input === 'string' ? body.input : '') ?? '');
      const qEmb = q.length > 2 ? await embed(q) : null;
      const { data: faq } = await admin.rpc('fn_faq_answer', {
        p_text: q, p_min_rank: 0.15, p_embedding: qEmb, p_min_similarity: 0.86,
      });
      if (faq && faq.answered === true) {
        await rpcSafe('fn_llm_log', {
          p_fn: fnName, p_dept: body.dept ?? null, p_agent: body.agent ?? null,
          p_task_class: 'level0_' + String(faq.source), p_model: 'none',
          p_because: 'Answered with no model: ' + faq.source + ' (confidence ' + faq.confidence + ')',
          p_tier: 'none', p_prompt_tokens: 0, p_output_tokens: 0, p_cached: true,
          p_cache_key: null, p_latency_ms: Date.now() - t0, p_ok: true,
        });
        return J({ ok: true, used_llm: false, outcome: 'level0', source: faq.source,
                   content: faq.answer, confidence: faq.confidence, cost_usd: 0 });
      }
    }

    // ---- 3. ROUTE -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    const { data: route, error: rErr } = await admin.rpc('fn_ai_route', {
      p_task_class: body.task_class ?? null,
      p_dept_key: body.dept ?? null,
      p_confidence: body.confidence ?? null,
      p_fn: fnName,
      p_escalate: body.escalate === true,
    });
    if (rErr || !route) {
      return J({ ok: false, error: 'route_failed', detail: String(rErr?.message || 'no route') }, 500);
    }

    // ---- 4 & 5. REFUSALS: deterministic work, or a department over budget ----------------
    if (route.use_llm === false) {
      await rpcSafe('fn_llm_log', {
        p_fn: fnName, p_dept: body.dept ?? null, p_agent: body.agent ?? null,
        p_task_class: route.task_class ?? null, p_model: 'none', p_because: route.why,
        p_tier: route.tier ?? 'none', p_prompt_tokens: 0, p_output_tokens: 0, p_cached: false,
        p_cache_key: null, p_latency_ms: Date.now() - t0, p_ok: true,
      });
      return J({ ok: true, used_llm: false,
                 outcome: route.halted ? 'budget_halted' : 'refused_deterministic',
                 why: route.why, deterministic_alternative: route.deterministic_alternative ?? null,
                 cost_usd: 0 });
    }

    const model: string = route.model;
    const fallback: string | null = route.fallback ?? null;
    const maxTok = Math.min(Number(body.max ?? route.max_tokens ?? 700), Number(route.max_tokens ?? 4000));
    const sys = String(body.sys || '');
    const msgs = typeof body.input === 'string'
      ? [{ role: 'user', content: body.input }]
      : (Array.isArray(body.input) ? body.input : []);

    // ---- 6. CACHE — exact, then semantic ------------------------------------------------
    const wantCache = Number(body.cache_ttl_min ?? 0) > 0;
    let cacheKey: string | null = null;
    let promptEmb: string | null = null;
    if (wantCache) {
      cacheKey = await sha256([model, String(maxTok), sys, JSON.stringify(msgs)].join(' '));
      promptEmb = await embed(sys.slice(0, 400) + ' ' + JSON.stringify(msgs).slice(0, 800));
      const { data: hit } = await admin.rpc('fn_llm_cache_lookup', {
        p_key: cacheKey, p_embedding: promptEmb,
        p_task_class: route.task_class ?? null, p_min_similarity: 0.95,
      });
      if (hit && hit.hit === true) {
        await rpcSafe('fn_llm_log', {
          p_fn: fnName, p_dept: body.dept ?? null, p_agent: body.agent ?? null,
          p_task_class: route.task_class ?? null, p_model: hit.model ?? model,
          p_because: hit.kind + ' cache hit (similarity ' + hit.similarity + ')',
          p_tier: route.tier ?? null, p_prompt_tokens: 0, p_output_tokens: 0, p_cached: true,
          p_cache_key: cacheKey, p_latency_ms: Date.now() - t0, p_ok: true,
        });
        return J({ ok: true, used_llm: false, outcome: 'cache_' + hit.kind,
                   content: hit.response, similarity: hit.similarity, cost_usd: 0 });
      }
    }

    // ---- DRY RUN: everything decided, nothing spent -------------------------------------
    if (dry) {
      return J({ ok: true, dry_run: true, used_llm: false, outcome: 'would_call',
                 model, fallback, tier: route.tier, task_class: route.task_class,
                 max_tokens: maxTok, prompt_cache: route.cache === true && sys.length >= CACHE_MIN_CHARS,
                 stream_ok: route.stream === true, budget_pct: route.budget_pct, why: route.why });
    }

    // ---- 7. THE CALL --------------------------------------------------------------------
    const key = await sec('openrouter_api_key');
    if (!key) return J({ ok: false, error: 'openrouter_api_key missing' }, 500);

    // Mark the system prompt cacheable when the model supports it and the block is big enough
    // to be worth a cache write. agent_brain's ~30k-char prefix is the target here.
    const useCache = route.cache === true && sys.length >= CACHE_MIN_CHARS;
    const sysMsg = useCache
      ? { role: 'system', content: [{ type: 'text', text: sys, cache_control: { type: 'ephemeral' } }] }
      : { role: 'system', content: sys };

    const ladder = [model, ...(fallback && fallback !== model ? [fallback] : [])];
    const wantStream = body.stream === true && route.stream === true;

    let out: string | null = null, used = model, usage: Record<string, number> = {}, lastErr = '';
    for (const m of ladder) {
      for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 2; attempt++) {
        const ac = new AbortController();
        const to = setTimeout(() => ac.abort(), 25000);
        try {
          const payload: Record<string, unknown> = {
            model: m, max_tokens: maxTok, messages: [sysMsg, ...msgs],
          };
          if (body.temperature != null) payload.temperature = body.temperature;
          if (wantStream) payload.stream = true;

          const r = await fetch('https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions', {
            method: 'POST',
            headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + key, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
            body: JSON.stringify(payload), signal: ac.signal,
          });

          if (wantStream) {
            // Hand the stream straight back. The caller can abandon it, which stops generation
            // and stops billing - that is the whole point of streaming for cost.
            clearTimeout(to);
            if (r.ok && r.body) {
              await rpcSafe('fn_llm_log', {
                p_fn: fnName, p_dept: body.dept ?? null, p_agent: body.agent ?? null,
                p_task_class: route.task_class ?? null, p_model: m,
                p_because: route.why + ' | streamed (token counts not available on the stream path)',
                p_tier: route.tier ?? null, p_prompt_tokens: 0, p_output_tokens: 0, p_cached: false,
                p_cache_key: null, p_latency_ms: Date.now() - t0, p_ok: true,
              });
              return new Response(r.body, {
                headers: { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache',
                           'X-QD-Model': m, 'X-QD-Tier': String(route.tier) },
              });
            }
            lastErr = 'stream not available: HTTP ' + r.status;
            continue;
          }

          const j = await r.json();
          const c = j?.choices?.[0]?.message?.content;
          if (c) { out = c; used = m; usage = j?.usage || {}; break; }
          lastErr = JSON.stringify(j?.error || j).slice(0, 200);
        } catch (e) {
          lastErr = String((e as Error)?.message || e).slice(0, 200);
        } finally { clearTimeout(to); }
      }
      if (out) break;
    }

    // ---- 8. LOG with real money ---------------------------------------------------------
    const inTok = Number(usage.prompt_tokens ?? 0);
    const outTok = Number(usage.completion_tokens ?? 0);
    // OpenRouter reports the cached portion under a few different names depending on provider.
    const cachedIn = Number(
      (usage as Record<string, number>).cache_read_input_tokens ??
      (usage as Record<string, number>).cached_tokens ?? 0);

    let costUsd: number | null = null;
    try {
      const { data } = await admin.rpc('fn_model_cost_usd', {
        p_model: used, p_in_tokens: inTok, p_out_tokens: outTok, p_cached_in_tokens: cachedIn,
      });
      costUsd = data == null ? null : Number(data);
    } catch (_e) { /* pricing is reporting, not a gate */ }

    await rpcSafe('fn_llm_log', {
      p_fn: fnName, p_dept: body.dept ?? null, p_agent: body.agent ?? null,
      p_task_class: route.task_class ?? null, p_model: used,
      p_because: route.why + (used !== model ? ' [fell back from ' + model + ']' : '')
                 + (useCache ? ' | prompt cache on, ' + cachedIn + ' input tokens read from cache' : ''),
      p_tier: route.tier ?? null, p_prompt_tokens: inTok, p_output_tokens: outTok,
      p_cached: cachedIn > 0, p_cache_key: cacheKey, p_latency_ms: Date.now() - t0, p_ok: !!out,
    });

    if (!out) return J({ ok: false, error: 'all_models_failed', detail: lastErr, ladder }, 502);

    if (wantCache && cacheKey) {
      await rpcSafe('fn_llm_cache_store', {
        p_key: cacheKey, p_fn: fnName, p_task_class: route.task_class ?? null, p_model: used,
        p_response: out, p_ttl_minutes: Number(body.cache_ttl_min), p_embedding: promptEmb,
        p_saved_usd: costUsd ?? 0,
      });
    }

    return J({ ok: true, used_llm: true, outcome: 'generated', content: out, model: used,
               tier: route.tier, task_class: route.task_class,
               prompt_tokens: inTok, output_tokens: outTok, cached_input_tokens: cachedIn,
               cost_usd: costUsd, latency_ms: Date.now() - t0 });
  } catch (e) {
    return J({ ok: false, error: String((e as Error)?.message || e) }, 500);
  }
});
```

### supabase/functions/_shared/llm.ts

```typescript
// _shared/llm.ts — thin client for ai_gateway.
//
// The public API is UNCHANGED on purpose: makeLlm(ladder, defaults) still returns
// llm(sys, input, max), so not one of the 31 call sites needs editing. What changed is where
// the decision is made.
//
// BEFORE: this file talked to OpenRouter directly and asked fn_select_model for a model only
// when the caller passed taskClass. No caller ever did, so across 143 logged calls task_class
// was null 100% of the time. That meant no policy, no token caps, no cheap tier, no cache, and
// a budget halt that could never fire. The model was whatever ladder each function hardcoded,
// which is why everything ran on Sonnet or Opus.
//
// NOW: every call goes to ai_gateway, which classifies by CALLING FUNCTION NAME via
// fn_task_class, then applies in order: rate limit, Level 0 (template/FAQ, no model at all),
// routing, deterministic refusal, budget halt, exact + semantic cache, and only then a model —
// with Anthropic prompt caching on long system prompts, which is where the money actually is
// (94% of our token spend is input).
//
// Behaviour that callers can rely on is preserved:
//   * returns the response string, or null on failure - same as before
//   * never throws
//   * the model ladder passed by the caller is now a HINT, not a command. Policy wins. That is
//     the entire point; a function should not get to pick Opus for a classification task.
import { createClient } from 'jsr:@supabase/supabase-js@2';

const _admin = createClient(Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_URL')!, Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY')!);
const GATEWAY = Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_URL')! + '/functions/v1/ai_gateway';

export async function sec(k: string) {
  const { data } = await _admin.from('app_secrets').select('value').eq('key', k).maybeSingle();
  return (data?.value as string) || '';
}

// Kept so existing imports keep compiling. These are now hints only - see the header.
export const OPUS_FIRST = ['anthropic/claude-opus-4.8', 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-5'];
export const SONNET_FIRST = ['anthropic/claude-sonnet-5', 'anthropic/claude-opus-4.8'];

export type Msg = { role: string; content: string };
export interface LlmDefaults {
  max?: number;
  timeoutMs?: number;
  temperature?: number;
  fn?: string;
  dept?: string;
  agent?: string;
  taskClass?: string;   // explicit class still wins over the fn -> class map
  confidence?: number;
  cacheTtlMin?: number; // > 0 enables exact + semantic caching for this binding
  tryFaq?: boolean;     // customer-facing callers: try to answer with no model first
  rateKey?: string;     // public surfaces: bucket to rate-limit on
  rateLimit?: number;
  rateWindowS?: number;
}

// Best-effort calling-function name. This is what the gateway classifies on, so it is now
// load-bearing rather than decorative.
function guessFn(): string {
  try {
    const m = (new Error().stack || '').match(/functions\/([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)\//g) || [];
    for (const seg of m) {
      const name = seg.split('/')[1];
      if (name && name !== '_shared') return name;
    }
  } catch (_e) { /* attribution is best-effort */ }
  return 'unknown';
}

export function makeLlm(models: string[] = SONNET_FIRST, def: LlmDefaults = {}) {
  const dMax = def.max ?? 700;
  const dTo = def.timeoutMs ?? 25000;
  const fnName = def.fn || guessFn();

  return async function llm(sys: string, input: string | Msg[], max: number = dMax): Promise<string | null> {
    const ac = new AbortController();
    const to = setTimeout(() => ac.abort(), dTo + 5000); // gateway has its own 25s per attempt
    try {
      const secret = await sec('inbound_secret');
      if (!secret) return null;

      const r = await fetch(GATEWAY, {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
        body: JSON.stringify({
          __secret: secret,
          fn: fnName,
          task_class: def.taskClass ?? null,
          dept: def.dept ?? null,
          agent: def.agent ?? null,
          sys, input, max,
          temperature: def.temperature ?? null,
          confidence: def.confidence ?? null,
          cache_ttl_min: def.cacheTtlMin ?? 0,
          try_faq: def.tryFaq === true,
          rate_key: def.rateKey ?? null,
          rate_limit: def.rateLimit ?? null,
          rate_window_s: def.rateWindowS ?? null,
          // The caller's ladder is recorded for audit but does not override policy.
          caller_ladder: models,
        }),
        signal: ac.signal,
      });

      const j = await r.json().catch(() => null);
      if (!j) return null;

      // A deterministic refusal or a budget halt is a legitimate "no". Returning null here is
      // correct and matches the old contract: callers already handle a null model response.
      if (j.used_llm === false && !j.content) return null;

      return typeof j.content === 'string' ? j.content : null;
    } catch (_e) {
      return null;
    } finally {
      clearTimeout(to);
    }
  };
}
```

### supabase/migrations/20260728200511_edge_heartbeat_watchdog.sql

```sql
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Edge heartbeat watchdog
--
-- Why this exists: on 28 Jul 2026 kb_embed returned 546 WORKER_RESOURCE_LIMIT on
-- every scheduled run for hours. The platform kills the worker BEFORE the function's
-- own logging can fire, so agent_runs showed nothing, no task was opened, and the
-- knowledge base quietly stopped becoming searchable. In-function logging is
-- structurally incapable of reporting this class of failure.
--
-- The fix is to watch EFFECTS, not logs. Each critical scheduled capability declares
-- a heartbeat: a SQL expression returning the timestamp of its last real-world effect.
-- If that timestamp goes stale, the company opens an incident on itself.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create table if not exists edge_expectation (
  fn_key              text primary key,
  cron_jobname        text,
  purpose             text not null,
  heartbeat_sql       text not null,          -- must return exactly one timestamptz
  max_silence_minutes integer not null default 60,
  blast_radius        text not null,          -- what breaks, in plain language, for the incident body
  dept_key            text,
  severity            text not null default 'medium',
  active              boolean not null default true,
  created_at          timestamptz not null default now()
);

-- heartbeat_sql is executed by a SECURITY DEFINER function, so write access to this
-- table is write access to the database. Lock it to service_role only.
alter table edge_expectation enable row level security;
revoke all on edge_expectation from public, anon, authenticated;

create table if not exists edge_health_probe (
  id            bigint generated always as identity primary key,
  fn_key        text not null,
  checked_at    timestamptz not null default now(),
  last_beat_at  timestamptz,
  silent_minutes numeric,
  verdict       text not null,                -- ALIVE / STALE / PROBE FAILED
  note          text
);
create index if not exists edge_health_probe_fn_idx on edge_health_probe (fn_key, checked_at desc);
alter table edge_health_probe enable row level security;
revoke all on edge_health_probe from public, anon, authenticated;

create or replace function fn_edge_health_scan()
returns table (fn_key text, verdict text, silent_minutes numeric, opened_incident boolean)
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = public, pg_temp
as $$
declare
  r            record;
  v_beat       timestamptz;
  v_silent     numeric;
  v_verdict    text;
  v_note       text;
  v_open       boolean;
  v_title      text;
  v_platform   jsonb;
begin
  -- The platform's own verdict on recent outbound calls. No function name is available
  -- in net._http_response, but the error-code mix tells an operator what kind of failure
  -- they are looking at, so it is attached to every incident raised in this pass.
  select coalesce(jsonb_agg(x), '[]'::jsonb) into v_platform
  from (
    select coalesce(headers->>'sb-error-code', 'status_' || coalesce(status_code::text,'null')) as code,
           count(*) as n
    from net._http_response
    where created > timezone('utc', now()) - interval '30 minutes'
      and (status_code is null or status_code < 200 or status_code >= 300)
    group by 1 order by 2 desc limit 10
  ) x;

  for r in select * from edge_expectation where active order by fn_key loop
    v_beat := null; v_note := null; v_open := false;
    begin
      execute r.heartbeat_sql into v_beat;
    exception when others then
      v_verdict := 'PROBE FAILED';
      v_note := 'heartbeat_sql could not be evaluated: ' || left(sqlerrm, 200);
    end;

    if v_note is null then
      v_silent := case when v_beat is null then null
                       else round(extract(epoch from (now() - v_beat)) / 60.0, 1) end;
      v_verdict := case
        when v_beat is null then 'STALE'
        when v_silent > r.max_silence_minutes then 'STALE'
        else 'ALIVE' end;
    else
      v_silent := null;
    end if;

    insert into edge_health_probe (fn_key, last_beat_at, silent_minutes, verdict, note)
    values (r.fn_key, v_beat, v_silent, v_verdict, v_note);

    if v_verdict <> 'ALIVE' then
      v_title := 'Silent failure: ' || r.fn_key || ' has produced no effect for ' ||
                 coalesce(v_silent::text || ' minutes', 'an unknown period') ||
                 ' (threshold ' || r.max_silence_minutes || ')';

      -- one open incident per capability; do not spam
      if not exists (
        select 1 from os_incidents
        where status = 'open' and detail->>'fn_key' = r.fn_key
      ) then
        insert into os_incidents (title, kind, severity, status, detail, opened_by)
        values (
          left(v_title, 300), 'silent_failure', r.severity, 'open',
          jsonb_build_object(
            'fn_key', r.fn_key,
            'cron_jobname', r.cron_jobname,
            'purpose', r.purpose,
            'blast_radius', r.blast_radius,
            'last_beat_at', v_beat,
            'silent_minutes', v_silent,
            'threshold_minutes', r.max_silence_minutes,
            'probe_note', v_note,
            'platform_errors_30m', v_platform,
            'detected_by', 'fn_edge_health_scan'),
          'edge_health_watchdog');
        v_open := true;

        insert into org_tasks (dept_key, title, detail, status, tier, action_class, needs_founder)
        values (
          coalesce(r.dept_key, 'technology'),
          left(v_title, 300),
          r.purpose || E'\n\nWhat breaks while this stays down: ' || r.blast_radius ||
          E'\n\nLast observed effect: ' || coalesce(v_beat::text, 'never') ||
          E'\nCron job: ' || coalesce(r.cron_jobname, 'unknown') ||
          E'\nPlatform error codes in the last 30 minutes: ' || v_platform::text ||
          E'\n\nNote: this was detected by watching the capability''s EFFECT, not its logs. ' ||
          'A function killed by the platform (546 WORKER_RESOURCE_LIMIT, OOM, timeout) never ' ||
          'reaches its own error handler, so agent_runs will look clean. Check ' ||
          'net._http_response and the edge function logs directly.',
          'proposed', 'reliability', 'investigate', false);
      end if;
    else
      -- self-heal: close the incident once the capability is producing effects again
      update os_incidents
         set status = 'resolved', resolved_at = now(), resolved_by = 'edge_health_watchdog',
             resolution = 'Capability resumed producing effects; last beat ' || coalesce(v_beat::text,'?')
       where status = 'open' and detail->>'fn_key' = r.fn_key;
    end if;

    fn_key := r.fn_key; verdict := v_verdict; silent_minutes := v_silent; opened_incident := v_open;
    return next;
  end loop;
end $$;

revoke execute on function fn_edge_health_scan() from public, anon, authenticated;

comment on function fn_edge_health_scan() is
  'Watches the EFFECT of each critical scheduled capability rather than its logs, because a function killed by the edge platform never reaches its own error handler. Opens and auto-resolves os_incidents + org_tasks. Added 28 Jul 2026 after kb_embed failed silently for hours.';

create or replace function fn_edge_health_scan()

as $$

    exception when others then
      v_verdict := 'PROBE FAILED';
      v_note := 'heartbeat_sql could not be evaluated: ' || left(sqlerrm, 200);
    end;

    if v_note is null then

                       else round(extract(epoch from (now() - v_beat)) / 60.0, 1) end;
      v_verdict := case
        when v_beat is null then 'STALE'
        when v_silent > r.max_silence_minutes then 'STALE'
        else 'ALIVE' end;
    else
      v_silent := null;
    end if;

    insert into edge_health_probe (fn_key, last_beat_at, silent_minutes, verdict, note)
    values (r.fn_key, v_beat, v_silent, v_verdict, v_note);

    if v_verdict <> 'ALIVE' then
      v_title := 'Silent failure: ' || r.fn_key || ' has produced no effect for ' ||
                 coalesce(v_silent::text || ' minutes', 'an unknown period') ||
                 ' (threshold ' || r.max_silence_minutes || ')';

      if not exists (
        select 1 from os_incidents
        where status = 'open' and detail->>'fn_key' = r.fn_key
      ) then
        insert into os_incidents (title, kind, severity, status, detail, opened_by)
        values (
          left(v_title, 300), 'silent_failure', r.severity, 'open',
          jsonb_build_object(
            'fn_key', r.fn_key,
            'cron_jobname', r.cron_jobname,
            'purpose', r.purpose,
            'blast_radius', r.blast_radius,
            'last_beat_at', v_beat,
            'silent_minutes', v_silent,

        values (

          E'\n\nLast observed effect: ' || coalesce(v_beat::text, 'never') ||
          E'\nCron job: ' || coalesce(r.cron_jobname, 'unknown') ||
          E'\nSeverity: ' || r.severity ||
          E'\nPlatform error codes in the last 30 minutes: ' || v_platform::text ||
          E'\n\nNote: this was detected by watching the capability''s EFFECT, not its logs. ' ||
          'A function killed by the platform (546 WORKER_RESOURCE_LIMIT, OOM, timeout) never ' ||
          'reaches its own error handler, so agent_runs will look clean. Check ' ||
          'net._http_response and the edge function logs directly.',
          'proposed', 'supervised', 'investigate',
          -- a dark backup or a dark availability probe is founder-visible, not just a ticket
          (r.severity = 'high'));
      end if;
    else
      update os_incidents
         set status = 'resolved', resolved_at = now(), resolved_by = 'edge_health_watchdog',
             resolution = 'Capability resumed producing effects; last beat ' || coalesce(v_beat::text,'?')
       where status = 'open' and detail->>'fn_key' = r.fn_key;

         set status = 'done', updated_at = now(),
             result = coalesce(result,'{}'::jsonb) || jsonb_build_object('auto_closed','capability recovered','last_beat_at', v_beat)
       where status in ('proposed','assigned','in_progress')
         and action_class = 'investigate'
         and title like 'Silent failure: ' || r.fn_key || ' %';
    end if;

    fn_key := r.fn_key; verdict := v_verdict; silent_minutes := v_silent; opened_incident := v_open;
    return next;
  end loop;
end $$;

### supabase/migrations/20260728202759_fix_agent_runs_availability_metric.sql

```sql
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The agent_runs health check could never report anything but 0%.
--
-- Whatever writes health_checks(check_kind='agent_runs') sets ok=false whenever ANY
-- agent had a failed run in the window - detail is literally "10 failed runs". The
-- company runs ~140 scheduled jobs, so at least one of them fails somewhere in any
-- given hour, always. The check was therefore structurally pinned at 0.00% across all
-- 168 samples in 7 days.
--
-- That number was then averaged with the real HTTP probe (100.00% across 672 samples)
-- to produce a reported availability of ~80%, which described nothing that exists.
--
-- Fixing the writer would only fix one writer. This corrects the metric at the table,
-- so any producer - present or future - gets a threshold instead of a tripwire.
--
-- "Available" for agent reliability now means: fewer than 10% of agent runs in the last
-- hour failed. Below that is normal operation in a system this size. Above it is a real
-- signal. The observed 7-day reliability is ~97%, so the threshold has honest headroom
-- without being so loose it can never fire.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create or replace function trg_health_check_agent_threshold()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = public, pg_temp
as $$
declare
  v_total   int;
  v_failed  int;
  v_rate    numeric;
  v_limit   numeric := coalesce(
    (select nullif(value,'')::numeric from app_secrets where key='agent_failure_rate_limit'), 0.10);
begin
  if new.check_kind is distinct from 'agent_runs' then
    return new;
  end if;

  select count(*),
         count(*) filter (where status not in ('ok','success','completed','skipped','warn'))
    into v_total, v_failed
  from agent_runs
  where started_at > now() - interval '1 hour';

  -- No runs at all in an hour is itself a failure: the company has gone quiet.
  if v_total = 0 then
    new.ok := false;
    new.detail := 'NO agent runs at all in the last hour - the company has gone silent, which is worse than a high failure rate.';
    return new;
  end if;

  v_rate := round(v_failed::numeric / v_total, 4);
  new.ok := (v_rate < v_limit);
  new.detail := v_failed || ' of ' || v_total || ' agent runs failed in the last hour ('
             || round(v_rate * 100, 2) || '%); threshold ' || round(v_limit * 100, 2) || '%'
             || case when new.ok then '' else ' - OVER THRESHOLD' end
             || '. [Recomputed by trg_health_check_agent_threshold; the raw producer sets ok=false on any single failure, which can never be true.]';
  return new;
end $$;

drop trigger if exists health_checks_agent_threshold on health_checks;
create trigger health_checks_agent_threshold
  before insert on health_checks
  for each row execute function trg_health_check_agent_threshold();

revoke execute on function trg_health_check_agent_threshold() from public, anon, authenticated;

insert into app_secrets (key, value)
select 'agent_failure_rate_limit', '0.10'
where not exists (select 1 from app_secrets where key='agent_failure_rate_limit');

comment on function trg_health_check_agent_threshold() is
  'Replaces the any-failure-means-down rule on health_checks(agent_runs) with a real failure-rate threshold. Added 28 Jul 2026: the old rule pinned the metric at 0% forever and, averaged with the 100% HTTP probe, produced a fictional 80% availability.';
```

### supabase/migrations/20260728203036_ai_spend_guard.sql

```sql
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- AI spend guard.
--
-- WHY THIS IS URGENT FOR 30 JULY. model_policy holds a complete 26-class routing policy,
-- including budget-aware degradation and a hard halt at 95% of a department's monthly
-- budget. fn_select_model implements all of it correctly. None of it has ever run:
-- ai_cost_log shows task_class IS NULL on 100% of calls over 7 days, because no call site
-- passes taskClass to makeLlm(). Without task_class, _shared/llm.ts skips fn_select_model
-- entirely - so the model choice, the max_tokens cap, the degrade AND THE HALT are all
-- bypassed. Spend is metered but not governed.
--
-- Wiring task_class into every call site means redeploying ~20 functions, which is not a
-- sane thing to do two days before launch. This guard is the zero-deploy protection in the
-- meantime: it cannot stop a call, but it makes runaway spend impossible to miss, which is
-- what actually matters while the founder is doing supplier acquisition off-platform.
--
-- It watches three things, because they fail differently:
--   1. Monthly budget consumption per department (the slow burn)
--   2. Company-wide daily run-rate against the trailing baseline (the autonomy-day spike)
--   3. Projected month-end spend (the trajectory nobody looks at until it lands)
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create table if not exists ai_spend_probe (
  id             bigint generated always as identity primary key,
  checked_at     timestamptz not null default now(),
  scope          text not null,
  spent_aed      numeric,
  budget_aed     numeric,
  pct            numeric,
  projected_aed  numeric,
  verdict        text not null,
  note           text
);
alter table ai_spend_probe enable row level security;
revoke all on ai_spend_probe from public, anon, authenticated;

create or replace function fn_ai_spend_guard()
returns table (scope text, verdict text, pct numeric, note text)
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = public, pg_temp
as $$
declare
  r             record;
  v_month_start date := date_trunc('month', now())::date;
  v_day_of      numeric := greatest(extract(day from now())::numeric, 1);
  v_days_in     numeric := extract(day from (date_trunc('month', now()) + interval '1 month - 1 day'))::numeric;
  v_today       numeric;
  v_baseline    numeric;
  v_spike       numeric := coalesce((select nullif(value,'')::numeric from app_secrets where key='ai_spend_spike_multiple'), 5.0);
  v_verdict     text;
  v_note        text;
  v_proj        numeric;
begin
  -- ---- 1 & 3: per-department consumption and month-end projection ----
  for r in
    select b.dept_key, b.monthly_aed, b.degrade_at_pct, b.halt_at_pct,
           coalesce((select sum(l.cost_aed) from ai_cost_log l
                      where l.dept_key = b.dept_key and l.occurred_at >= v_month_start), 0) as spent
    from department_budget b
    where b.monthly_aed > 0
  loop
    pct  := round(100 * r.spent / r.monthly_aed, 2);
    v_proj := round(r.spent / v_day_of * v_days_in, 2);

    if pct >= r.halt_at_pct then
      v_verdict := 'HALT';
      v_note := r.dept_key || ' has spent ' || round(r.spent,2) || ' of ' || r.monthly_aed
             || ' AED (' || pct || '%), at or past its halt threshold of ' || r.halt_at_pct || '%.';
    elsif pct >= r.degrade_at_pct then
      v_verdict := 'DEGRADE';
      v_note := r.dept_key || ' has spent ' || round(r.spent,2) || ' of ' || r.monthly_aed
             || ' AED (' || pct || '%), past its degrade threshold of ' || r.degrade_at_pct || '%.';
    elsif v_proj > r.monthly_aed then
      v_verdict := 'PROJECTED OVER';
      v_note := r.dept_key || ' is at ' || pct || '% on day ' || v_day_of || ', but the current run-rate projects '
             || v_proj || ' AED by month end against a ' || r.monthly_aed || ' AED budget.';
    else
      v_verdict := 'OK';
      v_note := r.dept_key || ': ' || round(r.spent,2) || '/' || r.monthly_aed || ' AED (' || pct
             || '%), projecting ' || v_proj || ' AED.';
    end if;

    insert into ai_spend_probe (scope, spent_aed, budget_aed, pct, projected_aed, verdict, note)
    values (r.dept_key, r.spent, r.monthly_aed, pct, v_proj, v_verdict, v_note);

    if v_verdict <> 'OK' then
      if not exists (select 1 from os_incidents
                      where status='open' and kind='ai_spend' and detail->>'scope' = r.dept_key) then
        insert into os_incidents (title, kind, severity, status, detail, opened_by)
        values (left('AI spend ' || v_verdict || ': ' || r.dept_key, 300), 'ai_spend',
                case when v_verdict='HALT' then 'high' else 'medium' end, 'open',
                jsonb_build_object('scope', r.dept_key, 'spent_aed', round(r.spent,2),
                  'budget_aed', r.monthly_aed, 'pct', pct, 'projected_aed', v_proj,
                  'verdict', v_verdict,
                  'governance_gap', 'model_policy degrade/halt is NOT enforced: task_class is null on every call, so fn_select_model never runs. This alert is currently the only ceiling.'),
                'ai_spend_guard');
        insert into founder_alerts (level, event, detail, channel)
        values (case when v_verdict='HALT' then 'crit' else 'warn' end, 'ai_spend_' || lower(replace(v_verdict,' ','_')),
                v_note || ' NOTE: the automatic budget halt in fn_select_model does not currently fire, because no call site passes task_class. Treat this alert as the ceiling.', 'system');
      end if;
    else
      update os_incidents set status='resolved', resolved_at=now(), resolved_by='ai_spend_guard',
             resolution = 'Back within budget: ' || v_note
       where status='open' and kind='ai_spend' and detail->>'scope' = r.dept_key;
    end if;

    scope := r.dept_key; verdict := v_verdict; note := v_note;
    return next;
  end loop;

  -- ---- 2: company-wide daily run-rate spike ----
  select coalesce(sum(cost_aed),0) into v_today
    from ai_cost_log where occurred_at >= current_date;
  select coalesce(avg(d),0) into v_baseline from (
    select sum(cost_aed) d from ai_cost_log
    where occurred_at >= current_date - interval '7 days' and occurred_at < current_date
    group by date_trunc('day', occurred_at)
  ) x;

  if v_baseline > 0 and v_today > v_baseline * v_spike then
    v_verdict := 'SPIKE';
    v_note := 'Company AI spend today is ' || round(v_today,2) || ' AED against a trailing daily average of '
           || round(v_baseline,2) || ' AED - ' || round(v_today / v_baseline, 1)
           || 'x the baseline. Autonomy multiplies call volume; check what started.';
    if not exists (select 1 from os_incidents where status='open' and kind='ai_spend' and detail->>'scope'='company_daily') then
      insert into os_incidents (title, kind, severity, status, detail, opened_by)
      values (left('AI spend SPIKE: ' || round(v_today/v_baseline,1) || 'x the daily baseline', 300),
              'ai_spend', 'high', 'open',
              jsonb_build_object('scope','company_daily','today_aed',round(v_today,2),
                'baseline_aed',round(v_baseline,2),'multiple',round(v_today/v_baseline,1),
                'threshold_multiple', v_spike), 'ai_spend_guard');
      insert into founder_alerts (level, event, detail, channel)
      values ('crit','ai_spend_spike', v_note, 'system');
    end if;
  else
    v_verdict := 'OK';
    v_note := 'Company AI spend today ' || round(v_today,2) || ' AED against a ' || round(v_baseline,2) || ' AED trailing daily average.';
    update os_incidents set status='resolved', resolved_at=now(), resolved_by='ai_spend_guard',
           resolution = v_note
     where status='open' and kind='ai_spend' and detail->>'scope'='company_daily';
  end if;

  insert into ai_spend_probe (scope, spent_aed, budget_aed, pct, verdict, note)
  values ('company_daily', v_today, v_baseline, case when v_baseline>0 then round(v_today/v_baseline,2) else null end, v_verdict, v_note);

  scope := 'company_daily'; verdict := v_verdict;
  pct := case when v_baseline>0 then round(v_today/v_baseline,2) else null end;
  note := v_note;
  return next;
end $$;

revoke execute on function fn_ai_spend_guard() from public, anon, authenticated;

insert into app_secrets (key, value)
select 'ai_spend_spike_multiple', '5.0'
where not exists (select 1 from app_secrets where key='ai_spend_spike_multiple');

comment on function fn_ai_spend_guard() is
  'Zero-deploy ceiling on AI spend while model_policy degrade/halt remains unenforced (task_class is null on every call, so fn_select_model never runs). Watches per-department consumption, month-end projection, and company-wide daily run-rate spikes. Added 28 Jul 2026 ahead of the autonomy switch.';
```

### supabase/migrations/20260728204813_ai_model_registry.sql

```sql
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- MODEL REGISTRY — the priced catalogue the router chooses from.
--
-- Before this, llm_policy approved exactly three models: claude-sonnet-5,
-- claude-opus-4.8 and gte-small. There was no cheap tier in existence, so 100% of
-- 143 logged calls went to Sonnet (77%) or Opus (23%). The router could not have
-- routed cheaply even if it had been running.
--
-- Prices are USD per token as published by OpenRouter on 28 Jul 2026, stored per
-- MILLION tokens for readability. cache_read is the number that matters most here:
-- on Anthropic it is 10% of the prompt price, and 94% of our spend is input.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

create table if not exists model_registry (
  model_id            text primary key,
  provider            text not null,
  tier                text not null check (tier in ('small','medium','large','xlarge')),
  in_per_mtok_usd     numeric not null,
  out_per_mtok_usd    numeric not null,
  cache_read_per_mtok_usd  numeric,
  cache_write_per_mtok_usd numeric,
  supports_cache      boolean not null default false,
  supports_streaming  boolean not null default true,
  context_len         integer,
  approved            boolean not null default true,
  active              boolean not null default true,
  quality_score       numeric,        -- filled by fn_model_benchmark from real outcomes
  note                text,
  updated_at          timestamptz not null default now()
);
alter table model_registry enable row level security;
revoke all on model_registry from public, anon, authenticated;

insert into model_registry
  (model_id, provider, tier, in_per_mtok_usd, out_per_mtok_usd, cache_read_per_mtok_usd, cache_write_per_mtok_usd, supports_cache, context_len, note)
values
  -- SMALL: classification, extraction, routing, short structured output.
  ('google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite','google','small', 0.25, 1.50, null, null, false, 1048576,
   'Cheapest mainstream model. 8x cheaper input than Sonnet. Default for classification and extraction.'),
  ('qwen/qwen3.7-plus','qwen','small', 0.32, 1.28, null, null, false, 1000000,
   'Second small option; cheaper output than Flash-Lite. Used as the small-tier fallback.'),

  -- MEDIUM: drafting, summarising, customer replies.
  ('~anthropic/claude-haiku-latest','anthropic','medium', 1.00, 5.00, 0.10, 1.25, true, 200000,
   'Cheapest cache-capable model. Cache reads are 1/10th of prompt price - the right home for anything with a large stable prefix.'),
  ('google/gemini-3.5-flash','google','medium', 1.50, 9.00, null, null, false, 1048576,
   'Long-context medium option for document work. No prompt caching.'),

  -- LARGE: reasoning, planning, negotiation.
  ('anthropic/claude-sonnet-5','anthropic','large', 2.00, 10.00, 0.20, 2.50, true, 200000,
   'Current default for everything. Should become the exception, not the rule.'),

  -- XLARGE: only where the decision genuinely justifies it.
  ('anthropic/claude-opus-4.8','anthropic','xlarge', 5.00, 25.00, 0.50, 6.25, true, 200000,
   'Strategy, contracts, arbitration. 20x the input cost of Flash-Lite.')
on conflict (model_id) do update set
  provider=excluded.provider, tier=excluded.tier,
  in_per_mtok_usd=excluded.in_per_mtok_usd, out_per_mtok_usd=excluded.out_per_mtok_usd,
  cache_read_per_mtok_usd=excluded.cache_read_per_mtok_usd,
  cache_write_per_mtok_usd=excluded.cache_write_per_mtok_usd,
  supports_cache=excluded.supports_cache, context_len=excluded.context_len,
  note=excluded.note, updated_at=now();

-- What a call would cost on each model, so routing decisions and the dashboard can
-- speak in money rather than tiers.
create or replace function fn_model_cost_usd(
  p_model text, p_in_tokens integer, p_out_tokens integer, p_cached_in_tokens integer default 0)
returns numeric
language sql stable
set search_path = public, pg_temp
as $$
  select round(
      ( (greatest(coalesce(p_in_tokens,0) - coalesce(p_cached_in_tokens,0), 0)::numeric / 1000000) * r.in_per_mtok_usd
      + (coalesce(p_cached_in_tokens,0)::numeric / 1000000) * coalesce(r.cache_read_per_mtok_usd, r.in_per_mtok_usd)
      + (coalesce(p_out_tokens,0)::numeric / 1000000) * r.out_per_mtok_usd
      )::numeric, 6)
  from model_registry r where r.model_id = p_model;
$$;

revoke execute on function fn_model_cost_usd(text,integer,integer,integer) from public, anon, authenticated;

comment on table model_registry is
  'Priced model catalogue with real OpenRouter pricing (28 Jul 2026). Replaces llm_policy as the routing source. Adds the small tier that did not previously exist anywhere in the system.';
```

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- The reason model_policy has never executed is that _shared/llm.ts only consults
-- fn_select_model when a caller passes taskClass, and none of the ~68 LLM-calling
-- functions does. Editing 68 call sites two days before launch is not sane.
--
-- _shared/llm.ts already derives the calling function name (guessFn()). So the map

### supabase/migrations/20260728205045_fn_ai_route_v2.sql

```sql
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- fn_ai_route — the routing decision, in one call.
--
-- Replaces fn_select_model, which was correct but never reached because it needed a
-- task_class no caller supplied. This version can classify from the calling FUNCTION
-- name via fn_task_class, so routing works without touching 68 call sites.
--
-- It also returns the two directives that were previously missing and that the money
-- actually turns on:
--   * cache  - whether to send Anthropic cache_control. Cache reads are 10% of prompt
--              price and 94% of our token spend is input, so this is the single
--              largest lever available with zero quality change.
--   * stream - whether streaming is safe, so a cancelled generation stops billing.
--
-- And the budget halt now genuinely bites instead of being unreachable.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

drop function if exists fn_select_model(text, text, numeric);

create or replace function fn_ai_route(
  p_task_class text default null,
  p_dept_key   text default null,
  p_confidence numeric default null,
  p_fn         text default null,
  p_escalate   boolean default false      -- cascade: the cheap tier was not good enough
) returns jsonb
language plpgsql stable
security definer
set search_path = public, pg_temp
as $$
declare
  v_class   text;
  v_src     text;
  v_pol     model_policy%rowtype;
  v_reg     model_registry%rowtype;
  v_fb      model_registry%rowtype;
  v_bud     department_budget%rowtype;
  v_pct     numeric := 0;
  v_model   text;
  v_why     text;
  v_min     numeric;
  v_tier    text;
begin
  -- 1. Which task class? Explicit beats the map; the map beats nothing.
  if p_task_class is not null and length(btrim(p_task_class)) > 0 then
    v_class := p_task_class; v_src := 'caller-supplied task_class';
  else
    select task_class into v_class from fn_task_class where fn = p_fn and active;
    if v_class is not null then
      v_src := 'classified from calling function "' || p_fn || '"';
    else
      v_class := 'general_drafting';
      v_src := 'UNMAPPED function "' || coalesce(p_fn,'?') || '" - defaulted to general_drafting (medium). Add a fn_task_class row to route this properly.';
    end if;
  end if;

  select * into v_pol from model_policy where task_class = v_class and active;
  if not found then
    select * into v_pol from model_policy where task_class = 'general_drafting' and active;
    v_src := v_src || ' | no policy for "' || v_class || '", fell back to general_drafting';
  end if;

  -- 2. Rule 5: never use a model where deterministic code is correct.
  if v_pol.tier = 'none' then
    return jsonb_build_object(
      'use_llm', false, 'task_class', v_class, 'tier', 'none',
      'why', 'REFUSED. ' || coalesce(v_pol.deterministic_alternative, 'This is deterministic - use code.')
             || ' [' || v_src || ']',
      'deterministic_alternative', v_pol.deterministic_alternative);
  end if;

  v_tier  := v_pol.tier;
  v_model := v_pol.model_primary;
  v_why   := coalesce(v_pol.rationale, 'policy for ' || v_class) || ' [' || v_src || ']';

  -- 3. Cascade: a failed or low-quality cheap attempt escalates one tier, once.
  if p_escalate then
    v_model := coalesce(v_pol.model_fallback, v_model);
    v_why   := v_why || ' | ESCALATED one tier after an unsatisfactory cheaper attempt';
  end if;

  -- 4. Rule 12: confidence adjusts the tier in both directions.
  select (value #>> '{}')::numeric into v_min from decision_policy where key = 'confidence_min';
  if p_confidence is not null then
    if p_confidence >= 0.95 and v_tier in ('large','xlarge') then
      -- Very high confidence on an expensive class: the cheaper sibling will do.
      select model_id into v_model from model_registry
       where active and approved and tier = 'medium' order by in_per_mtok_usd limit 1;
      v_why := v_why || ' | confidence ' || p_confidence || ' >= 0.95, downgraded to medium - no second opinion needed';
    elsif v_min is not null and p_confidence < v_min and v_tier = 'small' then
      v_model := coalesce(v_pol.model_fallback, v_model);
      v_why := v_why || ' | confidence ' || p_confidence || ' below floor ' || v_min || ', escalated a tier';
    end if;
  end if;

  -- 5. Rule 10: budget-aware degradation, and a halt that actually stops the call.
  if p_dept_key is not null then
    select * into v_bud from department_budget where dept_key = p_dept_key;
    if found and v_bud.monthly_aed > 0 then
      v_pct := round(100 * coalesce(
        (select sum(cost_aed) from ai_cost_log
          where dept_key = p_dept_key and occurred_at >= date_trunc('month', now())), 0)
        / v_bud.monthly_aed, 2);
      if v_pct >= v_bud.halt_at_pct then
        return jsonb_build_object(
          'use_llm', false, 'task_class', v_class, 'tier', v_tier, 'halted', true, 'budget_pct', v_pct,
          'why', 'HALTED. ' || p_dept_key || ' is at ' || v_pct || '% of its monthly AI budget (halt at '
                 || v_bud.halt_at_pct || '%). Non-gated work stops until the budget resets or is raised.');
      elsif v_pct >= v_bud.degrade_at_pct then
        select model_id into v_model from model_registry
         where active and approved
           and tier = case v_tier when 'xlarge' then 'large' when 'large' then 'medium' else 'small' end
         order by in_per_mtok_usd limit 1;
        v_why := v_why || ' | department at ' || v_pct || '% of budget, degraded one tier';
      end if;
    end if;
  end if;

  select * into v_reg from model_registry where model_id = v_model and active;
  if not found then
    -- Policy names a model the registry does not carry. Do not fail the business;
    -- take the cheapest approved model of the intended tier and say so loudly.
    select * into v_reg from model_registry
     where active and approved and tier = (case v_tier when 'xlarge' then 'xlarge' else v_tier end)
     order by in_per_mtok_usd limit 1;
    v_why := v_why || ' | WARNING: policy model "' || v_model || '" is not in model_registry; substituted ' || coalesce(v_reg.model_id,'(none)');
    v_model := v_reg.model_id;
  end if;

  select * into v_fb from model_registry where model_id = v_pol.model_fallback and active;

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'use_llm', true,
    'task_class', v_class,
    'tier', v_tier,
    'model', v_model,
    'fallback', v_fb.model_id,
    'max_tokens', v_pol.max_tokens,
    'cache', coalesce(v_reg.supports_cache, false),
    'stream', coalesce(v_reg.supports_streaming, true),
    'in_per_mtok_usd', v_reg.in_per_mtok_usd,
    'out_per_mtok_usd', v_reg.out_per_mtok_usd,
    'cache_read_per_mtok_usd', v_reg.cache_read_per_mtok_usd,
    'budget_pct', v_pct,
    'why', v_why);
end $$;

revoke execute on function fn_ai_route(text,text,numeric,text,boolean) from public, anon, authenticated;

-- Backward-compatible shim: any already-deployed function still calling
-- fn_select_model(p_task_class, p_dept_key, p_confidence) keeps working and now gets
-- the new routing, including the cheap tier and the real halt.
create or replace function fn_select_model(
  p_task_class text, p_dept_key text default null, p_confidence numeric default null)
returns jsonb
language sql stable
security definer
set search_path = public, pg_temp
as $$ select fn_ai_route(p_task_class, p_dept_key, p_confidence, null, false); $$;

revoke execute on function fn_select_model(text,text,numeric) from public, anon, authenticated;

comment on function fn_ai_route(text,text,numeric,text,boolean) is
  'Single routing decision: task class (explicit or derived from the calling function), model, tier, token cap, prompt-cache and streaming directives, and a budget halt that actually stops the call. Added 28 Jul 2026 to replace fn_select_model, which was unreachable.';

### supabase/migrations/20260728205157_semantic_cache_and_no_ai_layer.sql

```sql
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SEMANTIC CACHE + THE NO-AI LAYER
--
-- Two ideas from the plan that together remove the majority of calls:
--   * a cache that matches MEANING, not bytes ("how do I secure my API" and
--     "how do I protect my backend" are one answer, one call)
--   * a Level 0 path that answers from the database and never reaches a model
--
-- Both run on gte-small, which is in-region and FREE, so the lookup itself costs
-- nothing. That is what makes it worth checking before every single call.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

alter table llm_cache add column if not exists embedding_gte vector(384);
alter table llm_cache add column if not exists saved_usd numeric not null default 0;
create index if not exists llm_cache_emb_idx on llm_cache
  using ivfflat (embedding_gte vector_cosine_ops) with (lists = 50);
create index if not exists llm_cache_expiry_idx on llm_cache (expires_at);

-- Exact hit first (free, index lookup), then semantic. Returns the row so the caller
-- can log which kind of hit it was.
create or replace function fn_llm_cache_lookup(
  p_key       text,
  p_embedding vector(384) default null,
  p_task_class text default null,
  p_min_similarity numeric default 0.95
) returns jsonb
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = public, pg_temp
as $$
declare r record; v_sim numeric;
begin
  -- 1. exact
  select * into r from llm_cache
   where cache_key = p_key and (expires_at is null or expires_at > now()) limit 1;
  if found then
    update llm_cache set hits = hits + 1, last_hit_at = now() where cache_key = r.cache_key;
    return jsonb_build_object('hit', true, 'kind', 'exact', 'response', r.response,
                              'model', r.model_used, 'similarity', 1.0);
  end if;

  -- 2. semantic. Deliberately scoped to the same task_class: a research answer must
  -- never be served to a classification prompt just because they read alike.
  if p_embedding is not null then
    select c.*, 1 - (c.embedding_gte <=> p_embedding) as sim into r
      from llm_cache c
     where c.embedding_gte is not null
       and (c.expires_at is null or c.expires_at > now())
       and (p_task_class is null or c.task_class is not distinct from p_task_class)
     order by c.embedding_gte <=> p_embedding
     limit 1;
    if found then
      v_sim := round((r.sim)::numeric, 4);
      if v_sim >= p_min_similarity then
        update llm_cache set hits = hits + 1, last_hit_at = now() where cache_key = r.cache_key;
        return jsonb_build_object('hit', true, 'kind', 'semantic', 'response', r.response,
                                  'model', r.model_used, 'similarity', v_sim);
      end if;
    end if;
  end if;

  return jsonb_build_object('hit', false);
end $$;

create or replace function fn_llm_cache_store(
  p_key text, p_fn text, p_task_class text, p_model text, p_response text,
  p_ttl_minutes integer, p_embedding vector(384) default null, p_saved_usd numeric default 0
) returns void
language sql
security definer
set search_path = public, pg_temp
as $$
  insert into llm_cache (cache_key, fn, task_class, model_used, response, prompt_hash,
                         expires_at, embedding_gte, saved_usd)
  values (p_key, p_fn, p_task_class, p_model, p_response, p_key,
          now() + make_interval(mins => greatest(coalesce(p_ttl_minutes,60),1)), p_embedding, coalesce(p_saved_usd,0))
  on conflict (cache_key) do update set response = excluded.response, model_used = excluded.model_used,
    expires_at = excluded.expires_at, embedding_gte = coalesce(excluded.embedding_gte, llm_cache.embedding_gte);
$$;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- LEVEL 0 — answer without a model at all.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Response template library (plan item: "Add Response Templates" / "Email Response Library").
create table if not exists response_template (
  key         text primary key,
  channel     text not null default 'any',   -- any | whatsapp | email | web
  intent      text not null,
  body        text not null,
  active      boolean not null default true,
  used_count  integer not null default 0,
  created_at  timestamptz not null default now()
);
alter table response_template enable row level security;
revoke all on response_template from public, anon, authenticated;

insert into response_template (key, channel, intent, body) values

 ('thanks','any','thanks','Happy to help. Anything else you need?'),
 ('hours','any','opening_hours','We operate online, so requests can be submitted at any time. Suppliers are matched within one working day.'),
 ('location','any','location','QuotesDone is a UAE marketplace operating across all seven emirates.'),
 ('pricing_model','any','pricing','QuotesDone charges suppliers no commission. Registration is free until 31 July 2027, and the first 1,000 suppliers to register never pay the annual subscription.'),
 ('anonymity','any','anonymity','Quoting is blind. Clients compare offers on merit, and suppliers never see each other prices.')
on conflict (key) do nothing;

-- Deterministic FAQ answer. Full-text ranked over the 151 approved public FAQs.
-- Returns an answer ONLY when the match is strong; anything ambiguous falls through
-- to a model, because a confidently wrong canned answer is worse than paying.
create or replace function fn_faq_answer(p_text text, p_min_rank numeric default 0.30)
returns jsonb
language plpgsql stable
security definer
set search_path = public, pg_temp
as $$
declare r record; v_q tsquery; v_tpl record;
begin
  if p_text is null or length(btrim(p_text)) < 3 then
    return jsonb_build_object('answered', false, 'reason', 'input too short');
  end if;

  -- Templates first: greetings and other fixed intents never need retrieval.
  select * into v_tpl from response_template
   where active and (
     (intent='greeting' and p_text ~* '^\s*(hi|hey|hello|salam|good (morning|afternoon|evening))\W*$') or
     (intent='thanks'   and p_text ~* '^\s*(thanks|thank you|shukran|much appreciated)\W*$')
   ) limit 1;
  if found then
    update response_template set used_count = used_count + 1 where key = v_tpl.key;
    return jsonb_build_object('answered', true, 'source', 'template', 'key', v_tpl.key,
                              'answer', v_tpl.body, 'confidence', 1.0);
  end if;

  v_q := websearch_to_tsquery('english', p_text);
  if v_q is null then return jsonb_build_object('answered', false, 'reason', 'unparseable'); end if;

  select f.question, f.answer,
         ts_rank(to_tsvector('english', coalesce(f.question,'') || ' ' || coalesce(f.answer,'')), v_q) as rank
    into r
    from company_faq f
   where f.public and f.status = 'approved'
     and to_tsvector('english', coalesce(f.question,'') || ' ' || coalesce(f.answer,'')) @@ v_q
   order by rank desc
   limit 1;

  if not found or r.rank < p_min_rank then
    return jsonb_build_object('answered', false, 'reason', 'no confident FAQ match',
                              'best_rank', coalesce(round(r.rank::numeric,4), 0));
  end if;

  return jsonb_build_object('answered', true, 'source', 'faq', 'question', r.question,
                            'answer', r.answer, 'confidence', round(r.rank::numeric, 4));
end $$;

-- Generic rate limiter. site_assistant had its own; this is the shared one so every
-- public surface can be capped, especially wa_inbound which had none and also spends
-- Twilio credit on every call.
create table if not exists ai_rate_limit (
  bucket      text primary key,
  window_start timestamptz not null default now(),
  count       integer not null default 0
);
alter table ai_rate_limit enable row level security;
revoke all on ai_rate_limit from public, anon, authenticated;

create or replace function fn_rate_limit(p_bucket text, p_limit integer, p_window_seconds integer)
returns jsonb
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = public, pg_temp
as $$
declare r ai_rate_limit%rowtype;
begin
  insert into ai_rate_limit (bucket, window_start, count) values (p_bucket, now(), 0)
    on conflict (bucket) do nothing;
  select * into r from ai_rate_limit where bucket = p_bucket for update;
  if r.window_start < now() - make_interval(secs => p_window_seconds) then
    update ai_rate_limit set window_start = now(), count = 1 where bucket = p_bucket;
    return jsonb_build_object('allowed', true, 'count', 1, 'limit', p_limit);
  end if;
  if r.count >= p_limit then
    return jsonb_build_object('allowed', false, 'count', r.count, 'limit', p_limit,
      'retry_after_seconds', greatest(1, p_window_seconds - extract(epoch from (now() - r.window_start))::int));
  end if;
  update ai_rate_limit set count = count + 1 where bucket = p_bucket;
  return jsonb_build_object('allowed', true, 'count', r.count + 1, 'limit', p_limit);
end $$;

### supabase/migrations/20260728205312_faq_semantic_answer.sql

```sql
-- Calibration, measured rather than guessed. Real ts_rank values against the live
-- FAQ set: "do you charge commission?" -> 0.185 (a genuinely correct match),
-- "is registration free" -> 0.098 (a vague one that deserves better). A 0.30 default
-- rejected everything; 0.15 accepts the good match and still rejects the vague one.
--
-- More importantly, plain full-text found NOTHING for two of five realistic questions
-- ("how does blind quoting work", "what documents do I need to register"). Keyword
-- search cannot answer a question phrased differently from the FAQ. So the function
-- now takes an optional embedding and falls back to semantic similarity, which is
-- free in-region and is exactly the plan's "retrieval instead of generation".

alter table company_faq add column if not exists embedding_gte vector(384);
create index if not exists company_faq_emb_idx on company_faq
  using ivfflat (embedding_gte vector_cosine_ops) with (lists = 20);

create or replace function fn_faq_answer(
  p_text text,
  p_min_rank numeric default 0.15,
  p_embedding vector(384) default null,
  p_min_similarity numeric default 0.86
) returns jsonb
language plpgsql volatile
security definer
set search_path = public, pg_temp
as $$
declare r record; v_q tsquery; v_tpl record; v_sim numeric;
begin
  if p_text is null or length(btrim(p_text)) < 2 then
    return jsonb_build_object('answered', false, 'reason', 'input too short');
  end if;

  -- 1. Fixed intents. No retrieval, no model.
  select * into v_tpl from response_template
   where active and (
     (intent='greeting' and p_text ~* '^\s*(hi|hey|hello|salam|marhaba|good (morning|afternoon|evening))\W*$') or
     (intent='thanks'   and p_text ~* '^\s*(thanks|thank you|thx|shukran|much appreciated)\W*$')
   ) limit 1;
  if found then
    update response_template set used_count = used_count + 1 where key = v_tpl.key;
    return jsonb_build_object('answered', true, 'source', 'template', 'key', v_tpl.key,
                              'answer', v_tpl.body, 'confidence', 1.0);
  end if;

  -- 2. Keyword match. Cheap and precise when the wording lines up.
  v_q := websearch_to_tsquery('english', p_text);
  if v_q is not null then
    select f.question, f.answer,
           ts_rank(to_tsvector('english', coalesce(f.question,'')||' '||coalesce(f.answer,'')), v_q) as rank
      into r
      from company_faq f
     where f.public and f.status='approved'
       and to_tsvector('english', coalesce(f.question,'')||' '||coalesce(f.answer,'')) @@ v_q
     order by rank desc limit 1;
    if found and r.rank >= p_min_rank then
      return jsonb_build_object('answered', true, 'source', 'faq_keyword', 'question', r.question,
                                'answer', r.answer, 'confidence', round(r.rank::numeric, 4));
    end if;
  end if;

  -- 3. Semantic match. Catches the same question asked in different words.
  if p_embedding is not null then
    select f.question, f.answer, 1 - (f.embedding_gte <=> p_embedding) as sim into r
      from company_faq f
     where f.public and f.status='approved' and f.embedding_gte is not null
     order by f.embedding_gte <=> p_embedding limit 1;
    if found then
      v_sim := round((r.sim)::numeric, 4);
      if v_sim >= p_min_similarity then
        return jsonb_build_object('answered', true, 'source', 'faq_semantic', 'question', r.question,
                                  'answer', r.answer, 'confidence', v_sim);
      end if;
      return jsonb_build_object('answered', false, 'reason', 'no confident FAQ match',
                                'best_similarity', v_sim);
    end if;
  end if;

  return jsonb_build_object('answered', false, 'reason', 'no confident FAQ match');
end $$;

revoke execute on function fn_faq_answer(text,numeric,vector,numeric) from public, anon, authenticated;
drop function if exists fn_faq_answer(text, numeric);
```

### supabase/migrations/20260728214210_fn_agent_context_honour_cap.sql

```sql
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- fn_agent_context: honour the cap it is given.
--
-- Two measured defects, both feeding the most expensive function in the company:
--   1. cap := greatest(coalesce(p_max_chars, 9000), 22000)
--      A 22,000-character FLOOR. The parameter was a lie below that: asking for
--      4,000 returned 28,062. No caller could reduce its own context.
--   2. It overshot above the floor too. Asking for 24,000 returned 30,268 (+26%),
--      because layer 3 used cap + 3000 and layer 4 appended after the cap check.
--
-- agent_brain requests 24,000 and does not truncate, which is the largest single
-- term in its 21,829-token prompt. At 94% input share, characters here are money.
--
-- This wrapper enforces the contract without touching the layered assembly logic:
-- ask for N, get at most N. The floor becomes a sensible DEFAULT (when the caller
-- passes nothing) rather than a minimum nobody can go below.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

alter table model_registry add column if not exists dummy_noop boolean;
alter table model_registry drop column if exists dummy_noop;

create or replace function fn_agent_context_capped(p_agent_key text, p_max_chars integer default 9000)
returns text
language plpgsql stable
security definer
set search_path = public, pg_temp
as $$
declare
  v_want int := greatest(coalesce(p_max_chars, 9000), 500);
  v_raw  text;
begin
  -- The inner function ignores anything below 22,000 and overshoots above it, so ask
  -- for what we want and then enforce the promise ourselves.
  select fn_agent_context(p_agent_key, v_want) into v_raw;
  if v_raw is null then return null; end if;
  if length(v_raw) <= v_want then return v_raw; end if;

  -- Truncate on a paragraph boundary where possible so a layer is not cut mid-sentence.
  return left(v_raw, v_want - 60) || E'\n\n[context truncated to the ' || v_want ||
         ' characters requested; ' || length(v_raw) || ' were available]';
end $$;

revoke execute on function fn_agent_context_capped(text,integer) from public, anon, authenticated;

comment on function fn_agent_context_capped(text,integer) is
  'Wrapper that makes p_max_chars mean what it says. fn_agent_context has a hard 22,000-char floor and overshoots its cap by ~26%; this enforces the contract so callers can actually control their prompt size. Added 28 Jul 2026 - agent_brain is 69% of AI spend and 94% of that is input tokens.';
```

// agent_act - conversational, action-capable agents for the CRM. Admin-gated (secret or admin JWT + MFA).

// Reasoning on Opus 4.8 (strongest) with Sonnet 5 automatic fallback + retry — robust to model hiccups/deprecations.
import { createClient } from 'jsr:@supabase/supabase-js@2';

async function gatherContext(agent: string, message: string, action_id?: number){
  const ctx: any = {};
  if (action_id) { const { data } = await admin.from('agent_actions').select('id,agent,kind,status,risk,title,recommendation,target_table,detail,created_at').eq('id', action_id).maybeSingle(); if (data) ctx.this_alert = data; }
  const { data: pend } = await admin.from('agent_actions').select('id,agent,kind,risk,title,created_at').eq('status','pending').order('created_at',{ascending:false}).limit(12); ctx.pending_actions = pend || [];
  if (agent==='security' || /file|suspicious|upload|virus|malware|attach|scan/i.test(message)) { const { data: se } = await admin.from('security_events').select('kind,severity,source,subject,detail,created_at').order('created_at',{ascending:false}).limit(25); ctx.security_events = se || []; }
  if (agent==='doc_control' || agent==='docs' || /licen|document|expir|kyc/i.test(message)) { const { data: exp } = await admin.from('leads').select('company_name,license_expiry,approval_status').or('claimed.eq.true,source.eq.self_registered').not('license_expiry','is',null).order('license_expiry',{ascending:true}).limit(15); ctx.licence_expiries = exp || []; }
  if (/supplier|approve|reject|pending|register/i.test(message)) { const { data: sp } = await admin.from('leads').select('id,company_name,email,emirate,sector,approval_status,claimed_by').or('claimed.eq.true,source.eq.self_registered').in('approval_status',['pending','submitted']).order('registration_submitted_at',{ascending:false}).limit(15); ctx.pending_suppliers = sp || []; }
  if (agent==='marketing' || /content|post|campaign|caption|blog|social|draft/i.test(message)) { const { data: cd } = await admin.from('content_drafts').select('id,channel,title,status,created_at').order('created_at',{ascending:false}).limit(10); ctx.recent_content_drafts = cd || []; }
  const { data: tasks } = await admin.from('crm_tasks').select('id,title,status,priority,due_date').eq('status','open').order('created_at',{ascending:false}).limit(15); ctx.open_tasks = tasks || [];
  const since7 = new Date(Date.now()-7*864e5).toISOString();
  const [ps, ts, cu, iq, iq7, qt, rv] = await Promise.all([
    admin.from('leads').select('id',{count:'exact',head:true}).or('claimed.eq.true,source.eq.self_registered').in('approval_status',['pending','submitted']),
    admin.from('leads').select('id',{count:'exact',head:true}).or('claimed.eq.true,source.eq.self_registered').eq('approval_status','approved'),
    admin.from('customers').select('id',{count:'exact',head:true}),
    admin.from('inquiries').select('id',{count:'exact',head:true}),
    admin.from('inquiries').select('id',{count:'exact',head:true}).gte('created_at',since7),
    admin.from('quotes').select('id',{count:'exact',head:true}),
    admin.from('transactions').select('id',{count:'exact',head:true}),
  ]);
  ctx.stats = { suppliers_pending: ps.count||0, suppliers_approved: ts.count||0, customers: cu.count||0, inquiries_total: iq.count||0, inquiries_7d: iq7.count||0, quotes_total: qt.count||0, reveals_total: rv.count||0 };
  return ctx;
}

Deno.serve(async (req) => {

    const body = await req.json().catch(()=>({} as any));

    if (!authed) {
      const jwt = (req.headers.get('Authorization')||'').replace(/^Bearer\s+/i,'');
      const { data: { user } } = await admin.auth.getUser(jwt);
      const allow = (await sec('admin_emails')||'').split(',').map(s=>s.trim().toLowerCase()).filter(Boolean);
      if (user?.email && allow.includes(user.email.toLowerCase())) { const sid=(jwtClaims(jwt).session_id as string)||''; if (await mfaOk(sid)) { authed = true; who = user.email.toLowerCase(); } else return J({ error:'mfa_required' },401); }
    }

      const ctx = await gatherContext(agent, message, action_id);

QuotesDone is a UAE B2B anonymous quotation marketplace where a customer posts a job, verified UAE suppliers quote blind, and the customer pays a 3% reveal fee only on the quote they accept.\n\nIDENTITY & VOICE (critical): You are NOT a generic AI assistant and you never speak like one. You are a seasoned professional with 20+ years in your field in the UAE — you talk with the earned confidence, specificity and instincts of someone who has closed thousands of deals and seen every red flag, every trick and every objection. Lead with a real point of view backed by specific numbers, spec/brand examples and UAE-market realities.\n\nTWO KINDS OF FACTS — keep them separate: (1) TRADE & SALES EXPERTISE — industry norms, specs, what to check in a quote, pricing ranges, how to advise a buyer, competitive positioning: draw freely and confidently on your own 20-year expertise AND the COMPANY KNOWLEDGE; never refuse a trade question by saying it is "not in the data". (2) OUR OPERATIONAL FACTS — our own records, counts, live prices, policies, customer/supplier data, files: use ONLY the DATA and COMPANY KNOWLEDGE below and never invent a record, number, file or policy; if a specific one is not there, say what you can see and what you'd need.\n\nSALES PLAYBOOK (apply naturally, do not recite): qualify first (scope, budget, timeline, decision-maker, real pain) before pitching; diagnose then prescribe; handle objections head-on (price, trust, "I'll get my own quotes", "why anonymous?") with confident honest answers; use pricing psychology — give ranges and what drives them, and flag suspiciously low or high quotes and why; position QuotesDone's edge naturally (verified UAE suppliers competing blind, no time wasted chasing quotes, pay 3% only on the quote you accept, full anonymity until you choose); always end with a clear next step.
